storyContext.story-029: _claimRewards banks failed stable/promo transfers (unclaimableStableOf / unclaimablePromoOf) instead of reverting
storyContext.story-030: pauseWithdraw removed from PhlimboV3 (CONFIRMED absent by grep)

findings.description: phUSD reward leg is minted on demand (phUSD.mint(beneficiary, pendingPhUSDAmount) at :863) with NO funded-budget cap. In _updatePool the phUSD accrual `phUSDReward = timeElapsed * phUSDPerSecond` (:814) is NOT bounded by any balance/budget, unlike the stable leg which is explicitly capped by rewardBalance at :799 (`toDistribute > rewardBalance ? rewardBalance`). phUSDPerSecond derives from totalStaked*desiredAPYBps (:930), so emission continues unbounded as long as APY>0. This is the recurring 'over-emission of phUSD' class the caller flagged.
presentMitigations: single _updatePool writer folds in exactly elapsed*rate
missingMitigations: No per-day / per-window emission cap on phUSD mint (contrast stable :799 rewardBalance cap)
phUSD mint not backed by a funded budget invariant
findings.reconcileWith: DEDUP-04 (phUSD uncapped-mint, previously SUPPRESSED as config-conditional with a re-emit-if-nonzero-APY trigger). Route to sanitizer/econ-scanner to confirm whether the story-029 banking change alters the suppression basis. Confidence is about whether this is reportable-now vs known-suppressed, not about severity.
references: known issue #7 (phUSD minting rights), known issue #10 (zero-APY supported)

findings.description: MasterChef/linear-depletion accumulator farm. Signatures accPhUSDPerShare / accStablePerShare / accPromoPerShare / promoDebt / _updatePool all present. This is the 'Linear-Depletion rate-drift' class the caller explicitly said NOT to suppress (recurring in this suite; V1 had the recompute-on-every-interaction bug). V2/V3 mitigation is present: rewardPerSecond is recomputed ONLY in collectReward (:639) and setDepletionDuration (:279), and _updatePool no longer recomputes rate (:807-809 comment). All stake/withdraw/claim call _updatePool at the head; rate setters call _updatePool at the OLD rate before mutating. Surfaced per directive despite mitigations appearing intact — routed for the reasoning tier to re-verify the settle-before-mutate ordering survives the story-029 banking edits.
presentMitigations: rate setters settle at old rate first (:271, :406, :427)
findings.note: Do NOT auto-suppress (caller directive + suite history). No concrete un-mitigated ordering defect found by pattern match alone; escalate to code-scanner/econ-scanner for confirmation.

manualReview.description: story-029 surface: _claimRewards now makes external token calls (phUSD.mint :863, _tryTransfer(rewardToken) :875, _tryTransfer(promoToken) :899) to `beneficiary`. In stake/withdraw/claim, _claimRewards is invoked BEFORE the caller realigns userInfo debts (stake :674-676, withdraw :720-722, claim :767-769) and BEFORE totalStaked mutation. If a beneficiary could re-enter a sibling that reads userInfo/totalStaked, stale-debt double-claim would be possible.
presentMitigations: OZ v5 ReentrancyGuard is a single shared lock across ALL guarded entry points (stake/withdraw/claim/collectReward/batchClaim/claimUnclaimable*), so cross-function reentry is blocked
_tryTransfer is a raw transfer with no ERC777-style inbound hook to phUSD/rewardToken (fixed trusted tokens)
missingMitigations: promoToken is owner-set arbitrary ERC20; if a future promo token had a transfer callback, the external call at :899 precedes caller debt realignment — but all reentry targets are nonReentrant, so still blocked
manualReview.note: Appears mitigated by the shared lock. Flagged because story-029 widened the external-call surface inside _claimRewards; reasoning tier should confirm no unguarded value-reading sibling exists.

manualReview.description: story-029 accounting-drift check: banked stable (totalUnclaimableStable, :607/:877) and banked promo (totalUnclaimableOf, :499/:903) are physically held but claimed already accrued out of rewardBalance/promoRewardBalance at _updatePool (:805/:840). The :789/:799 cap operates on rewardBalance (undistributed) only, so banked tokens are argued to be non-redistributable. finalizePromotion reserves the promo bank (:536-538) before sweeping leftover; emergencyTransfer/withdrawAll deliberately sweep banks (documented ejector-seat trade-off).
presentMitigations: banked amounts accrued out of rewardBalance before banking, so :799 cap won't redistribute them
promo bank reserved from finalizePromotion sweep via totalUnclaimableOf
no-redistribution regression test cited in :164 comment
missingMitigations: stable bank has no finalize-equivalent reserve (rewardToken never rotates and is not swept as routine leftover — argued safe)
manualReview.note: Design argument appears sound; routed so a reasoning/invariant tier can assert `physicalBalance == rewardBalance + totalUnclaimableStable + <settled-unpaid>` holds and no double-count exists.

manualReview.description: setDesiredAPY two-step preview/commit bounded by `block.number > pendingAPYBlockNumber + 100` (:246). Signatures block.number / 100 / pending present.
presentMitigations: commit branch requires bps == pendingAPYBps (re-supplied and compared), so the value is effectively snapshotted at preview
_updatePool() called at old rate before desiredAPYBps changes (:254)
manualReview.note: Known issue #1 (intentional two-step security feature). No third-party re-arm griefing path found (onlyOwner). Low.

manualReview.description: Boundary checks: `block.number > pendingAPYBlockNumber + 100` (:246) and `block.timestamp <= lastRewardTime` early-return in _updatePool (:785). Both boundary semantics appear intentional (100-block commit window; <= avoids re-accrual within same timestamp).
manualReview.note: One-unit difference carries no value/safety consequence here. Included only to satisfy no-silent-drop.

manualReview.description: All reward math uses floor integer division: pending = amount*acc/PRECISION - debt (:483/:861/:866/:892), accX += toDistribute*PRECISION/totalStaked (:802/:815/:839), rate = balance*PRECISION/duration. Rounding floors payouts, i.e. favours the protocol (dust retained).
presentMitigations: every rounding decision floors the user payout (protocol-favourable)
manualReview.note: No user-favourable or asymmetric round-trip found; no attacker-repeatable leak. Clean by inspection, routed for completeness.

manualReview.description: phUSDPerSecond = (totalStaked * desiredAPYBps) / 10000 / SECONDS_PER_YEAR (:930) performs two sequential divisions. For small totalStaked or low APY this can truncate phUSDPerSecond to 0, silently disabling phUSD emission.
presentMitigations: zero-APY / negligible-emission is a documented supported mode (known issue #10)
manualReview.note: Standard APY-per-second truncation; documented as supported. Low/QA at most.

manualReview.description: migrate() (:188) and PhlimboV3.batchClaim() (:479) iterate over user/staker sets. Both are chunked by maxIterations with monotone cursors.
presentMitigations: explicit maxIterations chunking + monotone cursor on both loops
migrator documents the 63/64 gas-starvation edge and provides owner skipCurrent backstop (:284)
manualReview.note: Mitigated by design; the residual gas-starvation concern is already a documented operational hazard, not a new pattern hit.

regressionAnchorsVerified.location: src/PhlimboV3.sol:834 (_updatePool phase gate `promoPhase != PromoPhase.Flushing`) + :992 (pendingPromo view mirror)
regressionAnchorsVerified.note: accPromoPerShare freeze during Flushing enforced at the accrual site. All _updatePool callers reachable while paused/flushing (collectReward, setDesiredAPY commit, setDepletionDuration) are gated. beginFlush's own final accrual runs while phase is still Active (unaffected). No regression.

pauseWithdraw absent (grep-confirmed). No remaining path mutates totalStaked without a preceding _updatePool. emergencyTransfer (:344) sweeps+pauses but touches no accrual state (ejector-seat by design). No emission-recompute-bypass survives the removal.
Reverting recipients bank into unclaimable via non-reverting _tryTransfer; whole per-user body is try/catch'd so a reverting position is skipped, not bricking the pass.
